To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of carbonyls‐stabilized onium ylides allows the synthesis of highly functionalized trifluoro‐substituted‐cyclopropanes.

we developed a general and efficient protocol for the synthesis of trifluoroacetylated cyclopropanols and cyclopropanecarboxylates by the reaction of carbonyl compounds with onium ylides in the presence of a base.
we developed a general and operationally simple method for the synthesis of trifluoroacetylated cyclopropanols and cyclopropanones in good yields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and application of onium ylides in organic synthesis.
the synthesis of trifluoroacetylated cyclopropanated compounds.
the development of new methods for the synthesis of cyclopropane derivatives, which are of great interest in medicinal chemistry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of carbonylsulfonium ylides in the presence of potassium carbonate as base is the method of choice to access the most highly substituted trifluoroacetylated cyclopropanation products.
the diastereocontrol in this reaction is not only dependent on the nature of both the electrophile and the ylide, but also on the employed base.
the diastereo‐ and enantioselectivities are strongly influenced by the nature of the employed base, the structure of the ylides, as well as the nature of the trifluoroacetylated aldehydes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to synthesize highly‐functionalized, trifluoroacetylated cyclopropanols in good yields under mild conditions.
the use of carbonyls‐stabilized onium ylides allows the synthesis of trifluoroacetylated cyclopropanated carbonyl compounds.
the use of carbonylated ammonium‐ and phosphonium ylides is a very useful tool for the preparation of trifluoromethyl‐substituted heterocycles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
onium ylides are versatile and useful tools for the synthesis of trifluoromethyl‐substituted molecules.
onium‐based trifluoromethyl carbanions can be used for the synthesis of cyclopropanated trifluoroacetate derivatives in a diastereoselection‐controlled manner.
the use of carbonylsulfonium ylides is the method of choice to obtain trifluoroacetylcyclopropanes in good yields and high diastereoseletivities.
